topic: Sentence Completion (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Basic Concept of Sentence Completion
sections.content: In Sentence Completion, the first part of a sentence is given and there is a blank at the end. From the given options, you must choose the phrase or clause that makes the sentence correct both in meaning and grammar.

sections.title: Cause and Effect Logic
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the cause in the first part of the sentence. Step 2: Think about the natural effect or result of that cause. Step 3: Choose the option that correctly expresses that result. Example: 'It started raining heavily, so __________.' Correct answer: 'we decided to stay inside the house.'

sections.title: Simple Contrast Sentences
sections.content: Step 1: Identify contrast words such as but, although, however. Step 2: Understand the meaning of the first part. Step 3: Choose an option that shows an opposite or unexpected situation. Example: 'Although he was very tired, __________.' Correct answer: 'he continued working until the task was finished.'

sections.title: Logical Continuation
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the situation described in the sentence. Step 2: Think about what would logically happen next in real life. Step 3: Choose the option that gives the most natural continuation. Example: 'She studied regularly for the exam, so __________.' Correct answer: 'she felt confident on the day of the test.'

sections.title: Grammar Consistency
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the subject and tense in the sentence. Step 2: Check whether the option follows the same tense and structure. Step 3: Choose the option that maintains grammatical flow.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Focusing only on grammar and ignoring the meaning. 2. Choosing an option that goes against the logic of the sentence. 3. Failing to recognize contrast words.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Sentence Completion, first understand the meaning of the sentence, then identify cause-effect or contrast, and finally check grammar consistency. The option that provides the most logical continuation is the correct answer.

tricks.title: Meaning First Rule
tricks.explanation: First understand the complete meaning of the sentence, then check the options.
tricks.example: The road was very slippery, so __________. → 'the driver slowed down the car.'

tricks.title: Cause → Effect Trick
tricks.explanation: If the first part gives a cause, think about the result.
tricks.example: He missed the bus, so __________. → 'he had to wait for the next one.'

tricks.title: Contrast Signal Trick
tricks.explanation: If you see words like but or although, choose the opposite or contrasting idea.
tricks.example: Although the weather was cold, __________. → 'the children continued playing outside.'

tricks.title: Real-Life Logic Trick
tricks.explanation: Think about what would naturally happen in real life.
tricks.example: She forgot to set the alarm, so __________. → 'she woke up late in the morning.'

tricks.title: Grammar Matching Trick
tricks.explanation: The tense and subject of the option must match the sentence.
tricks.example: He was very hungry, so __________. → 'he quickly finished his meal.'

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: Remove options that are grammatically or logically incorrect first.
tricks.example: If two options are illogical, it becomes easier to choose the correct one from the remaining options.

tricks.title: Connector Clue Trick
tricks.explanation: Connectors such as so, because, therefore reveal the logic of the sentence.
tricks.example: She practiced every day, so __________. → 'her performance improved steadily.'

tricks.title: Smooth Flow Trick
tricks.explanation: The option that creates the most natural reading flow is usually correct.
tricks.example: The lights suddenly went out, so __________. → 'everyone looked around in surprise.'
